Laboratory Work � Fundamental Software Design Principles
Oct 13, 2026 � Mukhammadamin Salokhiddinov
How to work
This laboratory work follows Lecture 3 and Practical 3 of Design of Software Systems: modularity, information hiding, abstraction, cohesion, coupling, separation of concerns, DRY, KISS and YAGNI. It has 39 questions in nine parts, Parts G to I being the extension for the third year, and every case is new: none repeats an example from the lecture or the practical.
Nothing is programmed. You read short pieces of Python, name what you see, and redesign on paper. Work alone, in your notebook or in a .docx. In redesign tasks write only class names and method names with parameters, no bodies. Draw boxes and arrows by hand where a question asks for them. Plan for about two to three hours for Parts A to F.

==========================
PART A - MODULARITY AND INFORMATION HIDING
==========================

Q1. One job, one sentence

(a) Two. Timetable - stores the lessons of a group. ReminderSender - sends SMS reminders to the students.
(b) One. Grades - computes the final mark of a student.
(c) Two. Auth - checks a password. LoginScreen - draws the login screen.

Q2. Cut a system into modules

Modules:
- Session: keeps the film session and its seat map.
- Seats: shows which seats of the chosen session are free.
- Ticket: sells a ticket for a session and records the sale.
- TicketPrint: prints a sold ticket with its QR code.
- SalesReport: at night counts how many tickets each film sold.

Arrows: Seats uses Session; Ticket uses Session; TicketPrint uses Ticket; SalesReport uses Ticket.

Module with the most arrows pointing at it: Ticket (two arrows: from TicketPrint and SalesReport).
Not a problem by itself: it is the central business object. It becomes a problem only if
Ticket keeps growing; then every small change touches many modules.

Q3. Where is the border wrong?

(a) Broken rule: a module must own one job, not one kind of syntax.
    Border: loops and checks belong inside the modules whose data they serve.
(b) Broken rule: data must have one owner.
    Border: balance lives in an Account module exposing deposit() and withdraw();
    Booking, Refund and Admin call these methods.
(c) Broken rule: one external dependency must have one boundary.
    Border: a Telegram module wraps the API; Booking, Report and Admin call it.
(d) Broken rule: things that change together belong together.
    Border: price and tax are one tariff rule set in one Pricing module; tax.py merges into it.

Q4. A parking lot with no secrets

Kind of coupling: content coupling - outside code reads and writes internal fields.

After places becomes a dict {place_number: car_number}:
- parking.places[12] = "01A123BC"  - looks correct: writing a dict entry happens to match
  the new representation, but it still skips any booking check.
- if None in parking.places:       - wrong and dangerous: the dict keys are place numbers,
  never None, so the condition is always false and the screen says there is a free place
  even when the parking is full.
- hours * parking.prices["car"]    - correct: the price table did not change.

Most dangerous: the free-place check. It does not crash; it silently gives a wrong answer,
so users keep trusting a lie - a loud crash, by contrast, is noticed and fixed at once.

Public interface:
- book(place_number, car_number) -> bool
- free_place() -> place number or None
- leave(car_number) -> bool
- price(vehicle_type, hours) -> sum

Two secrets: (1) how the places are stored (list, dict or anything else);
(2) the price table and how the cost is computed.

Q5. "Just give me the list"

No: get_places() would hand out the internal representation and create content coupling
with every screen. Instead I would add free_places() -> int (or is_free(n)), which returns
only the answer the screen needs.

==========================
PART B - ABSTRACTION
==========================

Q6. Three words students confuse

(a) encapsulation  (b) information hiding  (c) abstraction
(d) information hiding  (e) abstraction

Q7. Procedural or data abstraction?

(a) D  (b) P  (c) P  (d) D  (e) P  (f) D

What the caller does not know:
- P, print_certificate: how the certificate is laid out and produced.
- D, cart add/total: how the cart stores and computes its items.

Q8. Put the levels in order

Order from the user (highest) to the hardware (lowest): C, D, F, A, E, B.

C - the user taps Send:               knows the user wants to send this text;
                                      does not know about json, bytes or radio.
D - chat.send(chat_id, text):         knows which chat and text the user chose;
                                      does not know how the network is built.
F - Message.create(sender_id, text):  knows the structure of a message;
                                      does not know where the message physically goes.
A - http.post("/messages", json):     knows URL, JSON body, status codes;
                                      does not know who the user is or what a chat is.
E - socket.send(bytes):               knows ports, packets, bytes;
                                      does not know URLs, JSON, users, chats.
B - the Wi-Fi chip:                   knows radio signals and frames;
                                      does not know anything about the chat app.

Q9. One interface, two implementations

Nothing that uses the interface must change; only the line that constructs a Counter is
rewritten (the two versions have identical method signatures).

With one million words and 1,000 count() calls version 2 wins: version 1 scans the whole
list for every count() - about 1,000 x 1,000,000 comparisons; version 2 keeps a ready dict,
so each count() is one lookup.

The interface promises that the answer is correct. It says nothing about speed. That is
what lets the implementer replace the implementation: as long as every caller gets the
correct answer, the team may trade speed, memory and simplicity inside the class.

Q10. How much should the interface show?

(a) too much - everyone reads and writes the inside of the timer, including the admin
    writing timer.running = False.
(b) too little - the screen team must rebuild the remaining-time rule from the start time;
    that knowledge belongs to the timer.
(c) just enough - start(minutes), stop(), seconds_left() and is_finished() cover all needs
    with no internals exposed.

In (b) the rule broken a few months later is DRY: the remaining time is computed in two
places. People notice when the two copies disagree - for example after an exam rule change
one screen shows the wrong time.

Test of slide 24 applied to (c): tonight I could replace the stored countdown by a
recomputation from the start timestamp, and I could change how is_finished() is decided,
and no caller would have to hear about it - both details stay hidden behind the same
four methods.

==========================
PART C - COHESION
==========================

Q11. Name the cohesion

(a) make_thumbnail  - Sequential. Each step consumes the result of the previous one.
(b) end_of_day      - Temporal. Unrelated jobs that happen at the same moment.
(c) is_leap_year    - Functional. One tiny job and nothing else.
(d) class Misc      - Coincidental. Three unrelated helpers share only the file name.
(e) passport_summary- Communicational. All three calls work on the same passport.
(f) export(report, fmt) - Logical. Same kind of work, one branch chosen by a flag.
(g) register_for_exam - Procedural. Fixed steps of one workflow, no data passed between them.

Q12. Three versions, three levels

A: sequential. B: communicational - every call works on the same card, the order of the
warnings does not matter. C: procedural.

The one question: is the output of one line the input of the next line?
- yes -> sequential;
- no, but all lines work on the same piece of data -> communicational;
- fixed order but no data passed between lines -> procedural.

Temporal = the parts belong together only because they run at the same moment and share
nothing. Procedural = the parts are steps of one workflow that would run in this order
even in the middle of the day. Version C is procedural.

Q13. The "and" test on a real class

Sentence: Invoice adds lines, computes the total, converts itself into a PDF, e-mails the
customer and saves itself into the database - the word "and" appears three times, so the
class has at least four or five jobs.

Changes:
(a) the e-mail provider changes  -> email_to_customer
(b) the tax rate changes         -> total
(c) the database moves to PostgreSQL -> save_to_db
(d) the PDF must show the shop logo  -> to_pdf
Four different reasons to change.

Split (names and methods only):
- Invoice: add_line(product, qty); total()
- PdfFormatter: to_pdf(invoice)
- CustomerEmailer: send(invoice, address)
- InvoiceRepository: save(invoice)

Slide 30 signals and the evidence:
- The module is too long: 1,400 lines and about a hundred more every week.
- Many unrelated dependencies: it imports sqlite3, smtplib, reportlab and requests -
  four different worlds in one file.
- Methods that do not share data: half the methods use self.connection, the other half

- Many people change it for different reasons: in one month Aziza fixed the PDF,

Strongest signal: the split between self.connection and self.smtp users.

Q15. When is temporal cohesion acceptable?

It is acceptable when the only thing the parts have in common is the moment they run,
and each job itself lives in its own cohesive module: end_of_day() is then just a
scheduled trigger (slide 6). It is not acceptable when the jobs themselves are mixed
inside the same function.

Two concrete problems of the second version:
(1) the business rule (summing the day's sales) is written inline in the driver, so a

(2) storage and infrastructure are hard-coded (sqlite3.connect, smtp.send, lights.off),
    so changing the database or the message system means editing this one function
    that also turns off the lights.

(a) send_sms(user)        - Stamp: the whole User with 15 fields travels, only phone is used.
(b) bookings.csv with ;   - External: two modules depend on the same outside file format.
(c) area(width, height)   - Data: exactly the values needed are passed.
(d) db._connection...     - Content: Report reaches inside Database and uses its private part.
(e) CURRENT_USER global   - Common: both functions read and write the same global data.
(f) format_price(amount, style) - Control: the style flag picks the branch inside.

From the worst to the best: d (content), e (common), b (external), f (control),

create_user(name, is_admin) is data coupling: True/False becomes a stored attribute of

flag chooses which of two branches inside save() will run.

A reader of save(user, True) does not know what True means - upload where? overwrite

Q19. Who decides the messenger?

(1) it chooses the messenger (Telegram); (2) it owns the secret token;

(a) System, 3,000 lines, everyone imports it: low cohesion + high coupling - the worst corner.
(b) Five small classes + global SETTINGS: high cohesion + high coupling.
(c) Three unrelated utils files: low cohesion + low coupling.
(d) Order receives Pricing, Storage, Receipt: high cohesion + low coupling - the goal corner.

Change that moves (b) to the goal corner: make one Settings module the owner of the
dictionary and expose get(name) / set(name, value); the five classes then receive the
values they need as ordinary parameters, so no global shared state is left.

(b) KISS. Write return age >= 18.
(c) YAGNI. Build one role now; add the twelfth when a second real role appears.

Q22. Same code, different knowledge

I do not fully agree. The two functions serve different concerns with different owners
and names (shipping vs parking), so fee(x) would replace two clear names with one

real DRY item.

What to do with 2000: name it in each owning module - UZS_PER_KG and UZS_PER_HOUR - or
hold one named tariff constant in one place if the university really prices both with
the same table; the number itself must never be typed twice without a name.

Q23. YAGNI or simple good design?

Developer B breaks YAGNI; developer A is doing good design. A pays almost nothing today
(one messages.py) and removes a real cost later: when a second language does come, the
texts are already out of the code and moving them is cheap. B pays for an engine, a
picker and a download system today, with seven languages to test and maintain, while the
customer asked for one language - the cost is real now and the saving never arrives,
because features nobody asked for usually never get used.

Q25. Count the jobs

Jobs of book(): (1) checks whether the machine is free; (2) writes the busy state into
the global STATUS; (3) computes the price from the mode flag; (4) applies the resident
discount; (5) appends the booking to bookings.txt; (6) sends the Telegram notification;
(7) prints a confirmation - five or six jobs depending on whether pricing and discount
are counted as one.

Level of cohesion: coincidental, with a control flag for the mode. Reason: checking,
pricing, storage, notification and printing are unrelated jobs dragged together only by
the booking event.

Three different numbers are written directly inside book(): 8000, 6000 and 0.10 - and
8000 is written twice, in the wash and the wash+dry branch.

(b) the parameter mode         - Control coupling.

(d) the whole student object   - Stamp coupling (only 3 of its fields are used).

with "Machine is busy". Tomorrow it is the same: nothing clears STATUS and book() never
looks at the hour, so machine 3 is dead until the program restarts.

    release(machine, hour) -> bool

- PriceCalculator: price(mode, is_resident) -> sum

                       new - PriceCalculator only.

Why "only one class changes" is not good news: that one class is the laundry class that

Q30. The settings everybody reads

Coupling between settings.py and each of the three: common coupling - all four share one
mutable global dictionary.

Pairs that depend on each other without importing: cart.py and invoice.py (their outputs
must agree: the total rounded in the cart and the digits printed on the invoice lines),
and both of them with admin.py, because admin silently redefines the values they already
computed with.

Two wrong things the customer can see after switch_to_usd() at 10:01:
(1) totals of carts filled at 10:00 are printed in USD but rounded with 0 decimals - a
    soum amount displayed as whole dollars;
(2) the cart and the invoice of the same order can disagree, because each module rounds
    at the moment it reads the shared dictionary.

The one thing inside switch_to_usd() that allows an inconsistent read: the change is not
atomic - it writes two keys in two separate statements, so an unlucky reader can observe
currency = USD together with decimals = 0, a pair that does not belong together.

If decimals must become a rounding step, cart.py and invoice.py must be edited
(round(sum, n) and the .{n}f format both assume whole digits); if one module owned the
whole rule, zero outside files would change.

The owner (Prices) exposes at most four methods:
    round(amount) -> number
    format(amount) -> string
    currency() -> string
    set_rule(currency, step) - called only by the admin

After the change cart.py and invoice.py know nothing about currency: they handle plain
amounts and call the owner for rounding and formatting. Only the owner (through set_rule,
called by the admin function) may change the currency.

Q31. Data that only travels

All three calls (checkout -> confirm -> schedule) are stamp coupling: each passes the
whole Order while using none of it (checkout, confirm) or only two fields (schedule).
The functions that only carry data they do not use are checkout and confirm.

When order.address becomes order.addresses: only schedule() must change, because it is
the only function that touches the address; checkout and confirm are unchanged. The
function that should have been the only one to know about addresses is schedule.

Rewrite so each function receives only what it uses:
    def checkout(payment) -> confirm(payment)                  - 1 parameter
    def confirm(payment)  -> schedule(payment)                 - 1 parameter
    def schedule(city, weight_kg) -> delivery_date(city, weight_kg) - 2 parameters
    def delivery_date(city, weight_kg)                         - 2 parameters
(In real code checkout and confirm, which add nothing, would collapse and disappear.)

Choosing between six values and the Order object: six separate values keep data coupling
but the call contracts grow - every time Order gains a field somebody must update the
parameter lists. Passing the Order is stamp coupling - schedule and confirm stay aware
of the whole type and break whenever its shape changes. Cost of the data choice: long
parameter lists and their maintenance; cost of the stamp choice: the whole call chain is
welded to the Order class.

Q32. Fewer arrows, more surprises

Version 1 knows 3 modules (fines, notifier, stats); version 2 knows 1 abstraction
(its listeners).

Version 2 still couples to its listeners by data coupling - they read named fields of
the same Loan object. If Loan loses the field they read, all three listeners break at
the same call (the first loop iteration raises AttributeError inside return_book).

Order: version 1 shows it literally in the body (close -> check -> tell -> record).
Version 2 hides it inside the subscription order. A bug possible only in version 2: an
out-of-order or duplicated subscription - for example a listener subscribed twice or
after the notifier, so the next reader is told the book is free before the fine is
recorded, or receives two notifications.

Two listeners that never change: keep version 1 - three explicit lines are cheaper to
write, read and debug than a subscription mechanism.
Twelve listeners written by five teams: version 2 - adding a listener then requires no
change to Loans, so the teams do not edit, build and conflict on one shared module.

Q33. The loop of imports

Import arrows: orders -> inventory (reserve), inventory -> pricing (stock_value),
pricing -> orders (Order). To test one file alone it must be importable without the
others: orders needs inventory and pricing; inventory needs pricing; pricing needs
orders - and through that, all three. Because of the loop, none of them can be tested
alone.

To ship pricing.py as a separate package, the Order class must travel with it (a copy or
a shared base/protocol), because pricing imports it.

First way - move one function: move stock_value() from pricing.py into inventory.py.
    Arrows after: orders -> inventory -> (nothing); pricing -> orders. Loop broken.
    Test order: inventory alone, orders with inventory, pricing with orders.

Second way - change what discount() receives:
    def discount(level): return 0.1 if level == "gold" else 0.0
    Arrows after: orders -> inventory -> pricing -> (nothing);
    the caller passes order.customer.level.

Order from knows nothing to knows the most (second way): pricing, inventory, orders.
This gives the build a fixed bottom-up sequence and gives each module unit tests that
run against nothing but the layer below it - in a loop no such order exists.

Q34. One rule, five places

Pieces of knowledge and the files holding them:
- A number is valid: +998 and 9 more digits, 13 characters -
  registration.py (the regex), sms.py (len == 13), schema.sql (code + length),
  test_data.py (13-character examples).
- A number has a leading + that must be stripped for the external gateway - sms.py.
- Public display rule: first 4 shown, rest masked - receipt.py.
- Two concrete valid formats as examples - test_data.py.

No line is copied - the knowledge is repeated.

Kazakhstan (+7, 12 characters): four places must be edited (registration.py, sms.py,
schema.sql, test_data.py). The one that will be forgotten is test_data.py, because it is
the least visible; the error shows up later - valid new numbers are rejected in
production, or valid production numbers are rejected by an old test.

Owner module PhoneNumbers:
    is_valid(phone) -> bool
    digits_only(phone) -> string
    mask(phone) -> string
    COUNTRY_CODE (constant)

The place that cannot use it: schema.sql - a database check is plain SQL and cannot
import a module, so the CHECK stays a deliberate copy.

Is the remaining database check a DRY violation? No - a deliberate copy at a trust
boundary is correct: the database protects against every future writer (other services,
manual inserts), not just this module. Add one test that pushes a valid and an invalid
number through both the module and the schema, so the two copies cannot silently drift
apart.

Q35. DRY gone too far

The flags create control coupling; the cohesion of calculate() is coincidental - nothing
holds its parts together except one entry point. A caller can ask for 2^4 = 16
behaviours; the three callers use 3.

The author followed DRY (one function for all variants) and broke KISS (a four-flag
switchboard instead of clear names) and separation of concerns (pricing, tax, rounding
and notification in one body).

Redesign - the smallest shared piece and the three callers on top:
    def sum_products(items): return sum(i.price * i.qty for i in items)  # the only
                                                                         # shared piece
    def quote(items):   return sum_products(items)
    def invoice(items): return round_up(apply_tax(sum_products(items)))
    def refund(items):  return -apply_tax(sum_products(items))
    notification is a separate call made by whoever needs it.
    Flags left: zero.

Pairs:
(a) two functions checking the 13-character phone: extract one shared validator - it is
    the same knowledge about one format.
(b) two four-line loops summing prices and weights: keep both - they are unrelated
    copies of a pattern that will diverge; extracting saves nothing and costs a shared
    dependency.

Q36. When two principles disagree

(a) DRY vs decoupling / release independence. My choice: keep two copies - sharing welds
    two releases together. The fact that would make me change sides: if the law required
    the invoices of both services to use one identical VAT value at every moment, one
    shared owner would be right.
(b) KISS vs separation of concerns. My choice: keep the script. The fact that would make
    me change sides: if it becomes a monthly process that several people edit and must
    not break, the split earns its cost.
(c) Information hiding vs performance. My choice: keep the secret; fix performance
    inside. The fact that would make me change sides: if no internal change can be fast
    enough, the Cache has to publish a new bulk operation - an interface change, not a
    public list.

(c) Change that keeps the secret and removes the slowness: add one public bulk method,
    for example read_entries(batch_size) or an internal index, that reads a million
    entries through a controlled method while the storage layout stays private.

Q37. The arrows point the wrong way

Import arrows: screens -> rules -> storage (the natural direction), and storage ->
screens - the wrong arrow: Storage knows the presentation and raises an Exception
carrying Uzbek error text.

Concerns inside the wrong modules: storage.py contains presentation (the Uzbek message);
rules.py contains presentation (HTML with <p class='red'>); screens.py adds none of its

Telegram bot in Russian: the new bot module must copy the call structure and the
knowledge of the cases (found / not found, debt), because the business result is only
available as Uzbek-shaped HTML; it either parses that HTML or repeats the rule work with

Redesign (no text, no HTML):
    storage.find_student(student_id) -> row/dict or raises StudentNotFound
    rules.check_in(student_id, room) -> Allowed(room) or Denied(reason),
                                        machine reasons like "debt"
    screens.check_in_page(form) -> maps Allowed/Denied to Uzbek HTML;
                                   the bot maps the same verdict to Russian

The texts now live in the presentation modules themselves (screens.py for Uzbek, the bot
for Russian); the business rules return only reason codes.

storage; screens.py may know about rules; storage.py may know about none of the others.

Q38. Audit the code

Evidence - copying the exact problem lines for five of the seven areas:
- Cohesion: the whole return_book body - it checks, computes, discounts, caps, stores,
  e-mails and prints in one method.
- Coupling: FINES = []  # global - common coupling (plus the CSV contract with
  MonthlyReport).
- Separation of concerns: the rule (days_late * 500, gold / 2, cap by book.price), the
  file write and email.send(...) live together in one method.
- DRY: the CSV format written here (reader.name + ',' + ... + str(fine)) and separately
  re-invented by MonthlyReport's line split.
- YAGNI: total_fines() - nothing in the story or the code ever calls it.

Two areas with no evidence in this code: information hiding and KISS.
- Information hiding: no outside module touches the private work of Library - nothing is
  exposed beyond the two methods and the shared files, so there is no line to cite.
- KISS: every individual rule line (fine = days_late * 500, the gold halving, the cap)
  is as simple as the rule itself - the mess of this code is cohesion, coupling and
  duplicated knowledge, not over-complex logic.
I do not invent a problem for them because an audit that stretches for missing evidence
would itself be dishonest - the honest answer is that these two principles are currently
satisfied.

A book titled "Algorithms, Part 1": the stored line contains a comma inside the title,
so MonthlyReport's split produces more than three parts and the report crashes with a
ValueError (too many values to unpack). Kind of coupling: external - two modules depend
on the same outside file format. Which module is at fault and why "neither" is the
better answer: the Library writes without quoting and MonthlyReport splits without
escaping, so each module is locally reasonable; the real fault is the missing owner of
the storage format - a rule (no unquoted commas, or a quoted CSV) that belongs to a
design decision written nowhere, so blaming one module is less accurate than saying the
format has no owner.

Restart difference: FINES is an in-process list, so after a restart total_fines() sums
from zero while month_total("fines.csv") still counts every stored fine - two truths
about one data set. Root cause: DRY (the same data is stored in two different places,
one of which is not durable).

Three changes in an order that keeps the program working after every step:
1. Write the fine record with proper quoting (csv.writer or a separator that cannot
   appear in titles) and read it the same way in MonthlyReport - this alone fixes the
   crash for titles like "Algorithms, Part 1", the most visible failure today.
2. Make one store the single source of truth: the file (via a small Ledger/Repository)
   is written and read by everyone; FINES is removed or rebuilt from the store, so
   total_fines() and the report can never disagree after a restart.
3. Keep money as whole-sum integers: replace fine = fine / 2 with an integer operation
   (for example (days_late * 500) // 2 capped at the book price) so no receipt ever
   shows a fractional sum.

+Lab 3 - Fundamental Software Design Principles
+Student: Albert Muratbaev
+
+==========================
+PART A - MODULARITY AND INFORMATION HIDING
+==========================
+
+Q1. One job, one sentence
+
+(a) Two. Timetable - stores the lessons of a group. ReminderSender - sends SMS reminders to the students.
+(b) One. Grades - computes the final mark of a student.
+(c) Two. Auth - checks a password. LoginScreen - draws the login screen.
+(d) One. Export - turns a finished report into a PDF file.
+
+Q2. Cut a system into modules
+
+Modules:
+- Session: keeps the film session and its seat map.
+- Seats: shows which seats of the chosen session are free.
+- Ticket: sells a ticket for a session and records the sale.
+- TicketPrint: prints a sold ticket with its QR code.
+- SalesReport: at night counts how many tickets each film sold.
+
+Arrows: Seats uses Session; Ticket uses Session; TicketPrint uses Ticket; SalesReport uses Ticket.
+
+Module with the most arrows pointing at it: Ticket (two arrows: from TicketPrint and SalesReport).
+Not a problem by itself: it is the central business object. It becomes a problem only if
+Ticket keeps growing; then every small change touches many modules.
+
+Q3. Where is the border wrong?
+
+(a) Broken rule: a module must own one job, not one kind of syntax.
+    Border: loops and checks belong inside the modules whose data they serve.
+(b) Broken rule: data must have one owner.
+    Border: balance lives in an Account module exposing deposit() and withdraw();
+    Booking, Refund and Admin call these methods.
+(c) Broken rule: one external dependency must have one boundary.
+    Border: a Telegram module wraps the API; Booking, Report and Admin call it.
+(d) Broken rule: things that change together belong together.
+    Border: price and tax are one tariff rule set in one Pricing module; tax.py merges into it.
+
+Q4. A parking lot with no secrets
+
+Kind of coupling: content coupling - outside code reads and writes internal fields.
+
+After places becomes a dict {place_number: car_number}:
+- parking.places[12] = "01A123BC"  - looks correct: writing a dict entry happens to match
+  the new representation, but it still skips any booking check.
+- if None in parking.places:       - wrong and dangerous: the dict keys are place numbers,
+  never None, so the condition is always false and the screen says there is a free place
+  even when the parking is full.
+- hours * parking.prices["car"]    - correct: the price table did not change.
+
+Most dangerous: the free-place check. It does not crash; it silently gives a wrong answer,
+so users keep trusting a lie - a loud crash, by contrast, is noticed and fixed at once.
+
+Public interface:
+- book(place_number, car_number) -> bool
+- free_place() -> place number or None
+- leave(car_number) -> bool
+- price(vehicle_type, hours) -> sum
+
+Two secrets: (1) how the places are stored (list, dict or anything else);
+(2) the price table and how the cost is computed.
+
+Q5. "Just give me the list"
+
+No: get_places() would hand out the internal representation and create content coupling
+with every screen. Instead I would add free_places() -> int (or is_free(n)), which returns
+only the answer the screen needs.
+
+==========================
+PART B - ABSTRACTION
+==========================
+
+Q6. Three words students confuse
+
+(a) encapsulation  (b) information hiding  (c) abstraction
+(d) information hiding  (e) abstraction
+
+Q7. Procedural or data abstraction?
+
+(a) D  (b) P  (c) P  (d) D  (e) P  (f) D
+
+What the caller does not know:
+- P, print_certificate: how the certificate is laid out and produced.
+- D, cart add/total: how the cart stores and computes its items.
+
+Q8. Put the levels in order
+
+Order from the user (highest) to the hardware (lowest): C, D, F, A, E, B.
+
+C - the user taps Send:               knows the user wants to send this text;
+                                      does not know about json, bytes or radio.
+D - chat.send(chat_id, text):         knows which chat and text the user chose;
+                                      does not know how the network is built.
+F - Message.create(sender_id, text):  knows the structure of a message;
+                                      does not know where the message physically goes.
+A - http.post("/messages", json):     knows URL, JSON body, status codes;
+                                      does not know who the user is or what a chat is.
+E - socket.send(bytes):               knows ports, packets, bytes;
+                                      does not know URLs, JSON, users, chats.
+B - the Wi-Fi chip:                   knows radio signals and frames;
+                                      does not know anything about the chat app.
+
+Q9. One interface, two implementations
+
+Nothing that uses the interface must change; only the line that constructs a Counter is
+rewritten (the two versions have identical method signatures).
+
+With one million words and 1,000 count() calls version 2 wins: version 1 scans the whole
+list for every count() - about 1,000 x 1,000,000 comparisons; version 2 keeps a ready dict,
+so each count() is one lookup.
+
+The interface promises that the answer is correct. It says nothing about speed. That is
+what lets the implementer replace the implementation: as long as every caller gets the
+correct answer, the team may trade speed, memory and simplicity inside the class.
+
+Q10. How much should the interface show?
+
+(a) too much - everyone reads and writes the inside of the timer, including the admin
+    writing timer.running = False.
+(b) too little - the screen team must rebuild the remaining-time rule from the start time;
+    that knowledge belongs to the timer.
+(c) just enough - start(minutes), stop(), seconds_left() and is_finished() cover all needs
+    with no internals exposed.
+
+In (b) the rule broken a few months later is DRY: the remaining time is computed in two
+places. People notice when the two copies disagree - for example after an exam rule change
+one screen shows the wrong time.
+
+Test of slide 24 applied to (c): tonight I could replace the stored countdown by a
+recomputation from the start timestamp, and I could change how is_finished() is decided,
+and no caller would have to hear about it - both details stay hidden behind the same
+four methods.
+
+==========================
+PART C - COHESION
+==========================
+
+Q11. Name the cohesion
+
+(a) make_thumbnail  - Sequential. Each step consumes the result of the previous one.
+(b) end_of_day      - Temporal. Unrelated jobs that happen at the same moment.
+(c) is_leap_year    - Functional. One tiny job and nothing else.
+(d) class Misc      - Coincidental. Three unrelated helpers share only the file name.
+(e) passport_summary- Communicational. All three calls work on the same passport.
+(f) export(report, fmt) - Logical. Same kind of work, one branch chosen by a flag.
+(g) register_for_exam - Procedural. Fixed steps of one workflow, no data passed between them.
+
+Q12. Three versions, three levels
+
+A: sequential. B: communicational - every call works on the same card, the order of the
+warnings does not matter. C: procedural.
+
+The one question: is the output of one line the input of the next line?
+- yes -> sequential;
+- no, but all lines work on the same piece of data -> communicational;
+- fixed order but no data passed between lines -> procedural.
+
+Temporal = the parts belong together only because they run at the same moment and share
+nothing. Procedural = the parts are steps of one workflow that would run in this order
+even in the middle of the day. Version C is procedural.
+
+Q13. The "and" test on a real class
+
+Sentence: Invoice adds lines, computes the total, converts itself into a PDF, e-mails the
+customer and saves itself into the database - the word "and" appears three times, so the
+class has at least four or five jobs.
+
+Changes:
+(a) the e-mail provider changes  -> email_to_customer
+(b) the tax rate changes         -> total
+(c) the database moves to PostgreSQL -> save_to_db
+(d) the PDF must show the shop logo  -> to_pdf
+Four different reasons to change.
+
+Split (names and methods only):
+- Invoice: add_line(product, qty); total()
+- PdfFormatter: to_pdf(invoice)
+- CustomerEmailer: send(invoice, address)
+- InvoiceRepository: save(invoice)
+
+Q14. Read the signals
+
+Slide 30 signals and the evidence:
+- The module is too long: 1,400 lines and about a hundred more every week.
+- Many unrelated dependencies: it imports sqlite3, smtplib, reportlab and requests -
+  four different worlds in one file.
+- Methods that do not share data: half the methods use self.connection, the other half
+  use self.smtp and never touch the database.
+- Many people change it for different reasons: in one month Aziza fixed the PDF,
+  Bekzod added an SMS provider, Dilnoza fixed a SQL query.
+- A meaningless name: DataProcessor says nothing about one job.
+
+Strongest signal: the split between self.connection and self.smtp users.
+Check in thirty seconds: search the file for which methods mention connection and which
+mention smtp - if the two sets of method names do not overlap, the class is really
+two classes.
+
+Q15. When is temporal cohesion acceptable?
+
+It is acceptable when the only thing the parts have in common is the moment they run,
+and each job itself lives in its own cohesive module: end_of_day() is then just a
+scheduled trigger (slide 6). It is not acceptable when the jobs themselves are mixed
+inside the same function.
+
+Two concrete problems of the second version:
+(1) the business rule (summing the day's sales) is written inline in the driver, so a
+    change of the rule touches a night job;
+(2) storage and infrastructure are hard-coded (sqlite3.connect, smtp.send, lights.off),
+    so changing the database or the message system means editing this one function
+    that also turns off the lights.
+
+==========================
+PART D - COUPLING
+==========================
+
+Q16. Name the coupling
+
+(a) send_sms(user)        - Stamp: the whole User with 15 fields travels, only phone is used.
+(b) bookings.csv with ;   - External: two modules depend on the same outside file format.
+(c) area(width, height)   - Data: exactly the values needed are passed.
+(d) db._connection...     - Content: Report reaches inside Database and uses its private part.
+(e) CURRENT_USER global   - Common: both functions read and write the same global data.
+(f) format_price(amount, style) - Control: the style flag picks the branch inside.

+From the worst to the best: d (content), e (common), b (external), f (control),
+a (stamp), c (data).

+Q17. Move one step down the table

+(a) Stamp -> data:

+Q18. The same boolean, two kinds of coupling

+create_user(name, is_admin) is data coupling: True/False becomes a stored attribute of
+the new user; no branch changes meaning. save(user, to_cloud) is control coupling: the
+flag chooses which of two branches inside save() will run.

+A reader of save(user, True) does not know what True means - upload where? overwrite
+what? The call says nothing about the target.

+Rewrite without a flag:
+    def save(user, storage): storage.write(user)

+Q19. Who decides the messenger?
+
+Three decisions AttendanceReport makes that are not its job:
+(1) it chooses the messenger (Telegram); (2) it owns the secret token;
+(3) it names the recipient @group_ce22.

+Wish 1 (e-mail instead of Telegram): the constructor and the body must be rewritten to

+sending - usually an if inside send(), which pushes test knowledge into production code.

+        def __init__(self, sender): ...
+        def send(self, text): self.sender.post(text)

+    for a test:   AttendanceReport(NullSender()) - a sender that contacts no network.
+
+Q20. Place it on the golden-rule square
+
+(a) System, 3,000 lines, everyone imports it: low cohesion + high coupling - the worst corner.
+(b) Five small classes + global SETTINGS: high cohesion + high coupling.
+(c) Three unrelated utils files: low cohesion + low coupling.
+(d) Order receives Pricing, Storage, Receipt: high cohesion + low coupling - the goal corner.
+
+Change that moves (b) to the goal corner: make one Settings module the owner of the
+dictionary and expose get(name) / set(name, value); the five classes then receive the
+values they need as ordinary parameters, so no global shared state is left.
+
+==========================
+PART E - SEPARATION OF CONCERNS, DRY, KISS, YAGNI
+==========================
+
+Q21. Which rule is broken?
+
+(a) DRY. One constant MAX_STUDENTS and one full-limit message live in group.py;
+    enroll.py and messages.py use them.
+(b) KISS. Write return age >= 18.
+(c) YAGNI. Build one role now; add the twelfth when a second real role appears.
+(d) Separation of concerns. Compute the price in a rule function, save through a
+    repository, show the result on the screen - three separate calls.
+(e) KISS. Write max(a, b, c).
+
+Q22. Same code, different knowledge
+
+I do not fully agree. The two functions serve different concerns with different owners
+and names (shipping vs parking), so fee(x) would replace two clear names with one
+flag-driven function - but the repeated knowledge inside them, the tariff 2000, is a
+real DRY item.
+
+What to do with 2000: name it in each owning module - UZS_PER_KG and UZS_PER_HOUR - or
+hold one named tariff constant in one place if the university really prices both with
+the same table; the number itself must never be typed twice without a name.
+
+Q23. YAGNI or simple good design?
+
+Developer B breaks YAGNI; developer A is doing good design. A pays almost nothing today
+(one messages.py) and removes a real cost later: when a second language does come, the
+texts are already out of the code and moving them is cheap. B pays for an engine, a
+picker and a download system today, with seven languages to test and maintain, while the
+customer asked for one language - the cost is real now and the saving never arrives,
+because features nobody asked for usually never get used.
+
+Q24. Sort the lines by concern
+
+(1) if balance < price: refuse()        - Business rules
+(2) INSERT INTO orders ...              - Storage
+(3) show_message(...)                   - Presentation
+(4) logger.info(...)                    - Infrastructure
+(5) discount = 0.1 if has_meal_card ... - Business rules
+(6) sms.send(phone, ...)                - Infrastructure
+(7) button.color = green                - Presentation
+(8) SELECT balance FROM wallets ...     - Storage
+
+A class named OrderScreen may contain only the Presentation concern; it must not write
+SQL, decide rules or send SMS itself.
+
+==========================
+PART F - CASE STUDY: THE DORMITORY LAUNDRY
+==========================
+
+Q25. Count the jobs
+
+Jobs of book(): (1) checks whether the machine is free; (2) writes the busy state into
+the global STATUS; (3) computes the price from the mode flag; (4) applies the resident
+discount; (5) appends the booking to bookings.txt; (6) sends the Telegram notification;
+(7) prints a confirmation - five or six jobs depending on whether pricing and discount
+are counted as one.
+
+Level of cohesion: coincidental, with a control flag for the mode. Reason: checking,
+pricing, storage, notification and printing are unrelated jobs dragged together only by
+the booking event.
+
+Three different numbers are written directly inside book(): 8000, 6000 and 0.10 - and
+8000 is written twice, in the wash and the wash+dry branch.
+
+Q26. Name every coupling
+
+(a) the global STATUS          - Common coupling.
+(b) the parameter mode         - Control coupling.
+(c) bookings.txt with ;        - External coupling: two modules depend on the same file
+                                 format (WeeklyReport also reads it).
+(d) the whole student object   - Stamp coupling (only 3 of its fields are used).
+(e) telegram.send(...) inside  - External coupling to a concrete device/service.
+
+Q27. Who owns STATUS?
+
+Rustam books machine 3 at 10:00; the entry stays forever, so Malika at 18:00 is refused
+with "Machine is busy". Tomorrow it is the same: nothing clears STATUS and book() never
+looks at the hour, so machine 3 is dead until the program restarts.
+
+The data must be owned by a schedule module (rule 2 of slide 15: one owner of the data).
+Call it MachineSchedule. Public interface:
+    book(machine, hour, student) -> bool
+    is_booked(machine, hour) -> bool
+    release(machine, hour) -> bool
+    bookings(machine) -> list
+
+After the change nobody else may write to that data: MachineSchedule is the single
+writer; every other module goes through its methods.
+
+Q28. Redesign on paper
+
+Classes (names and methods only):
+- MachineSchedule: book(machine, hour, student) -> bool; is_booked(machine, hour);
+                   bookings(machine)
+- PriceCalculator: price(mode, is_resident) -> sum
+- BookingRepository: append(booking); read_all() -> lines
+- TelegramNotifier: notify(telegram_id, text)
+- BookingService (the connector): receives schedule, calculator, repository, notifier
+  in its constructor; book(student, machine, hour, mode) -> receipt
+
+Boxes and arrows: BookingService points to the four classes; WeeklyReport points to
+BookingRepository. That is five arrows; counting them stops me from adding a sixth
+dependency (for example calling Telegram directly from the schedule).
+
+Where the numbers live now: 8000, 6000 and 0.10 all live inside PriceCalculator, and
+each is written exactly once.
+
+After the redesign the confirmation "Booked! Price: ..." is printed by the caller of
+BookingService - the screen or presentation module; the service itself only returns the
+price in a receipt.
+
+Q29. The two numbers
+
+(a) discount 15%:      old - the number 0.10 inside book();
+                       new - PriceCalculator only.
+(b) SMS instead of Telegram: old - the telegram.send call inside book() plus imports;
+                       new - replace the Notifier used by BookingService (one class,
+                       no service change).
+(c) SQLite instead of bookings.txt: old - book() file code AND WeeklyReport;
+                       new - add SqliteBookingRepository, the service is unchanged,
+                       WeeklyReport reads through the repository.
+(d) test with no messages and no files: old - nothing clean is possible, the test must
+                       fake telegram, files and stdout;
+                       new - pass NullNotifier and an in-memory repository into
+                       BookingService in the test.
+
+Why "only one class changes" is not good news: that one class is the laundry class that
+holds all the jobs, so every change is made inside the same crowded body, the file is a
+shared conflict point for every future wish, and nothing about the change can be tested
+in isolation.
+
+==========================
+PART G - COUPLING IN DEPTH
+==========================
+
+Q30. The settings everybody reads
+
+Coupling between settings.py and each of the three: common coupling - all four share one
+mutable global dictionary.
+
+Pairs that depend on each other without importing: cart.py and invoice.py (their outputs
+must agree: the total rounded in the cart and the digits printed on the invoice lines),
+and both of them with admin.py, because admin silently redefines the values they already
+computed with.
+
+Two wrong things the customer can see after switch_to_usd() at 10:01:
+(1) totals of carts filled at 10:00 are printed in USD but rounded with 0 decimals - a
+    soum amount displayed as whole dollars;
+(2) the cart and the invoice of the same order can disagree, because each module rounds
+    at the moment it reads the shared dictionary.
+
+The one thing inside switch_to_usd() that allows an inconsistent read: the change is not
+atomic - it writes two keys in two separate statements, so an unlucky reader can observe
+currency = USD together with decimals = 0, a pair that does not belong together.
+
+If decimals must become a rounding step, cart.py and invoice.py must be edited
+(round(sum, n) and the .{n}f format both assume whole digits); if one module owned the
+whole rule, zero outside files would change.
+
+The owner (Prices) exposes at most four methods:
+    round(amount) -> number
+    format(amount) -> string
+    currency() -> string
+    set_rule(currency, step) - called only by the admin
+
+After the change cart.py and invoice.py know nothing about currency: they handle plain
+amounts and call the owner for rounding and formatting. Only the owner (through set_rule,
+called by the admin function) may change the currency.
+
+Q31. Data that only travels
+
+All three calls (checkout -> confirm -> schedule) are stamp coupling: each passes the
+whole Order while using none of it (checkout, confirm) or only two fields (schedule).
+The functions that only carry data they do not use are checkout and confirm.
+
+When order.address becomes order.addresses: only schedule() must change, because it is
+the only function that touches the address; checkout and confirm are unchanged. The
+function that should have been the only one to know about addresses is schedule.
+
+Rewrite so each function receives only what it uses:
+    def checkout(payment) -> confirm(payment)                  - 1 parameter
+    def confirm(payment)  -> schedule(payment)                 - 1 parameter
+    def schedule(city, weight_kg) -> delivery_date(city, weight_kg) - 2 parameters
+    def delivery_date(city, weight_kg)                         - 2 parameters
+(In real code checkout and confirm, which add nothing, would collapse and disappear.)
+
+Choosing between six values and the Order object: six separate values keep data coupling
+but the call contracts grow - every time Order gains a field somebody must update the
+parameter lists. Passing the Order is stamp coupling - schedule and confirm stay aware
+of the whole type and break whenever its shape changes. Cost of the data choice: long
+parameter lists and their maintenance; cost of the stamp choice: the whole call chain is
+welded to the Order class.
+
+Q32. Fewer arrows, more surprises
+
+Version 1 knows 3 modules (fines, notifier, stats); version 2 knows 1 abstraction
+(its listeners).
+
+Version 2 still couples to its listeners by data coupling - they read named fields of
+the same Loan object. If Loan loses the field they read, all three listeners break at
+the same call (the first loop iteration raises AttributeError inside return_book).
+
+Order: version 1 shows it literally in the body (close -> check -> tell -> record).
+Version 2 hides it inside the subscription order. A bug possible only in version 2: an
+out-of-order or duplicated subscription - for example a listener subscribed twice or
+after the notifier, so the next reader is told the book is free before the fine is
+recorded, or receives two notifications.
+
+Two listeners that never change: keep version 1 - three explicit lines are cheaper to
+write, read and debug than a subscription mechanism.
+Twelve listeners written by five teams: version 2 - adding a listener then requires no
+change to Loans, so the teams do not edit, build and conflict on one shared module.
+
+Q33. The loop of imports
+
+Import arrows: orders -> inventory (reserve), inventory -> pricing (stock_value),
+pricing -> orders (Order). To test one file alone it must be importable without the
+others: orders needs inventory and pricing; inventory needs pricing; pricing needs
+orders - and through that, all three. Because of the loop, none of them can be tested
+alone.
+
+To ship pricing.py as a separate package, the Order class must travel with it (a copy or
+a shared base/protocol), because pricing imports it.
+
+First way - move one function: move stock_value() from pricing.py into inventory.py.
+    Arrows after: orders -> inventory -> (nothing); pricing -> orders. Loop broken.
+    Test order: inventory alone, orders with inventory, pricing with orders.
+
+Second way - change what discount() receives:
+    def discount(level): return 0.1 if level == "gold" else 0.0
+    Arrows after: orders -> inventory -> pricing -> (nothing);
+    the caller passes order.customer.level.
+
+Order from knows nothing to knows the most (second way): pricing, inventory, orders.
+This gives the build a fixed bottom-up sequence and gives each module unit tests that
+run against nothing but the layer below it - in a loop no such order exists.
+
+==========================
+PART H - SEPARATION OF CONCERNS, DRY, KISS, YAGNI IN DEPTH
+==========================
+
+Q34. One rule, five places
+
+Pieces of knowledge and the files holding them:
+- A number is valid: +998 and 9 more digits, 13 characters -
+  registration.py (the regex), sms.py (len == 13), schema.sql (code + length),
+  test_data.py (13-character examples).
+- A number has a leading + that must be stripped for the external gateway - sms.py.
+- Public display rule: first 4 shown, rest masked - receipt.py.
+- Two concrete valid formats as examples - test_data.py.
+
+No line is copied - the knowledge is repeated.
+
+Kazakhstan (+7, 12 characters): four places must be edited (registration.py, sms.py,
+schema.sql, test_data.py). The one that will be forgotten is test_data.py, because it is
+the least visible; the error shows up later - valid new numbers are rejected in
+production, or valid production numbers are rejected by an old test.
+
+Owner module PhoneNumbers:
+    is_valid(phone) -> bool
+    digits_only(phone) -> string
+    mask(phone) -> string
+    COUNTRY_CODE (constant)
+
+The place that cannot use it: schema.sql - a database check is plain SQL and cannot
+import a module, so the CHECK stays a deliberate copy.
+
+Is the remaining database check a DRY violation? No - a deliberate copy at a trust
+boundary is correct: the database protects against every future writer (other services,
+manual inserts), not just this module. Add one test that pushes a valid and an invalid
+number through both the module and the schema, so the two copies cannot silently drift
+apart.
+
+Q35. DRY gone too far
+
+The flags create control coupling; the cohesion of calculate() is coincidental - nothing
+holds its parts together except one entry point. A caller can ask for 2^4 = 16
+behaviours; the three callers use 3.
+
+The author followed DRY (one function for all variants) and broke KISS (a four-flag
+switchboard instead of clear names) and separation of concerns (pricing, tax, rounding
+and notification in one body).
+
+Redesign - the smallest shared piece and the three callers on top:
+    def sum_products(items): return sum(i.price * i.qty for i in items)  # the only
+                                                                         # shared piece
+    def quote(items):   return sum_products(items)
+    def invoice(items): return round_up(apply_tax(sum_products(items)))
+    def refund(items):  return -apply_tax(sum_products(items))
+    notification is a separate call made by whoever needs it.
+    Flags left: zero.
+
+Pairs:
+(a) two functions checking the 13-character phone: extract one shared validator - it is
+    the same knowledge about one format.
+(b) two four-line loops summing prices and weights: keep both - they are unrelated
+    copies of a pattern that will diverge; extracting saves nothing and costs a shared
+    dependency.
+
+Q36. When two principles disagree
+
+(a) DRY vs decoupling / release independence. My choice: keep two copies - sharing welds
+    two releases together. The fact that would make me change sides: if the law required
+    the invoices of both services to use one identical VAT value at every moment, one
+    shared owner would be right.
+(b) KISS vs separation of concerns. My choice: keep the script. The fact that would make
+    me change sides: if it becomes a monthly process that several people edit and must
+    not break, the split earns its cost.
+(c) Information hiding vs performance. My choice: keep the secret; fix performance
+    inside. The fact that would make me change sides: if no internal change can be fast
+    enough, the Cache has to publish a new bulk operation - an interface change, not a
+    public list.
+
+(c) Change that keeps the secret and removes the slowness: add one public bulk method,
+    for example read_entries(batch_size) or an internal index, that reads a million
+    entries through a controlled method while the storage layout stays private.
+
+Q37. The arrows point the wrong way
+
+Import arrows: screens -> rules -> storage (the natural direction), and storage ->
+screens - the wrong arrow: Storage knows the presentation and raises an Exception
+carrying Uzbek error text.
+
+Concerns inside the wrong modules: storage.py contains presentation (the Uzbek message);
+rules.py contains presentation (HTML with <p class='red'>); screens.py adds none of its
+own.
+
+Telegram bot in Russian: the new bot module must copy the call structure and the
+knowledge of the cases (found / not found, debt), because the business result is only
+available as Uzbek-shaped HTML; it either parses that HTML or repeats the rule work with
+its own Russian answer.
+
+Redesign (no text, no HTML):
+    storage.find_student(student_id) -> row/dict or raises StudentNotFound
+    rules.check_in(student_id, room) -> Allowed(room) or Denied(reason),
+                                        machine reasons like "debt"
+    screens.check_in_page(form) -> maps Allowed/Denied to Uzbek HTML;
+                                   the bot maps the same verdict to Russian
+
+The texts now live in the presentation modules themselves (screens.py for Uzbek, the bot
+for Russian); the business rules return only reason codes.
+
+Arrows after the change: screens -> rules -> storage = 2 arrows. rules.py may know about
+storage; screens.py may know about rules; storage.py may know about none of the others.
+
+==========================
+PART I - CASE STUDY: THE LIBRARY FINES
+==========================
+
+Q38. Audit the code
+
+Evidence - copying the exact problem lines for five of the seven areas:
+- Cohesion: the whole return_book body - it checks, computes, discounts, caps, stores,
+  e-mails and prints in one method.
+- Coupling: FINES = []  # global - common coupling (plus the CSV contract with
+  MonthlyReport).
+- Separation of concerns: the rule (days_late * 500, gold / 2, cap by book.price), the
+  file write and email.send(...) live together in one method.
+- DRY: the CSV format written here (reader.name + ',' + ... + str(fine)) and separately
+  re-invented by MonthlyReport's line split.
+- YAGNI: total_fines() - nothing in the story or the code ever calls it.
+
+Two areas with no evidence in this code: information hiding and KISS.
+- Information hiding: no outside module touches the private work of Library - nothing is
+  exposed beyond the two methods and the shared files, so there is no line to cite.
+- KISS: every individual rule line (fine = days_late * 500, the gold halving, the cap)
+  is as simple as the rule itself - the mess of this code is cohesion, coupling and
+  duplicated knowledge, not over-complex logic.
+I do not invent a problem for them because an audit that stretches for missing evidence
+would itself be dishonest - the honest answer is that these two principles are currently
+satisfied.
+
+A book titled "Algorithms, Part 1": the stored line contains a comma inside the title,
+so MonthlyReport's split produces more than three parts and the report crashes with a
+ValueError (too many values to unpack). Kind of coupling: external - two modules depend
+on the same outside file format. Which module is at fault and why "neither" is the
+better answer: the Library writes without quoting and MonthlyReport splits without
+escaping, so each module is locally reasonable; the real fault is the missing owner of
+the storage format - a rule (no unquoted commas, or a quoted CSV) that belongs to a
+design decision written nowhere, so blaming one module is less accurate than saying the
+format has no owner.

+Restart difference: FINES is an in-process list, so after a restart total_fines() sums
+from zero while month_total("fines.csv") still counts every stored fine - two truths
+about one data set. Root cause: DRY (the same data is stored in two different places,
+one of which is not durable).
+
+Three changes in an order that keeps the program working after every step:
+1. Write the fine record with proper quoting (csv.writer or a separator that cannot
+   appear in titles) and read it the same way in MonthlyReport - this alone fixes the
+   crash for titles like "Algorithms, Part 1", the most visible failure today.
+2. Make one store the single source of truth: the file (via a small Ledger/Repository)
+   is written and read by everyone; FINES is removed or rebuilt from the store, so
+   total_fines() and the report can never disagree after a restart.
+3. Keep money as whole-sum integers: replace fine = fine / 2 with an integer operation
+   (for example (days_late * 500) // 2 capped at the book price) so no receipt ever
+   shows a fractional sum.

--- page 1 ---
Python Classes/Objects 
Python is an object-oriented programming language. 
Almost everything in Python is an object, with its properties and methods. 
A Class is like an object constructor, or a "blueprint" for creating objects. 
 
Create a Class 
To create a class, use the keyword class: 
Example  
Create a class named MyClass, with a property named x: 
class MyClass: 
  x = 5 
 
Create Object 
Now we can use the class named MyClass to create objects: 
Example  
Create an object named p1, and print the value of x: 
p1 = MyClass() 
print(p1.x) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
--- page 2 ---
The __init__() Function 
The examples above are classes and objects in their simplest form, and are not really 
useful in real life applications. 
To understand the meaning of classes we have to understand the built-in __init__() 
function. 
All classes have a function called __init__(), which is always executed when the class is 
being initiated. 
Use the __init__() function to assign values to object properties, or other operations that 
are necessary to do when the object is being created: 
Example  
Create a class named Person, use the __init__() function to assign values for name and 
age: 
class Person: 
  def __init__(self, name, age): 
    self.name = name 
    self.age = age 
 
p1 = Person("John", 36) 
 
print(p1.name) 
print(p1.age) 
Note: The __init__() function is called automatically every time the class is being used 
to create a new object. 
 
The __str__() Function 
The __str__() function controls what should be returned when the class object is 
represented as a string. 
If the __str__() function is not set, the string representation of the object is returned: 
Example  
The string representation of an object WITHOUT the __str__() function: 
class Person: 
  def __init__(self, name, age): 
    self.name = name 
    self.age = age 
 
p1 = Person("John", 36) 
--- page 3 ---
 
print(p1) 
 
Example  
The string representation of an object WITH the __str__() function: 
class Person: 
  def __init__(self, name, age): 
    self.name = name 
    self.age = age 
 
  def __str__(self): 
    return f"{self.name}({self.age})" 
 
p1 = Person("John", 36) 
 
print(p1) 
 
Object Methods 
Objects can also contain methods. Methods in objects are functions that belong to the 
object. 
Let us create a method in the Person class: 
Example  
Insert a function that prints a greeting, and execute it on the p1 object: 
class Person: 
  def __init__(self, name, age): 
    self.name = name 
    self.age = age 
 
  def myfunc(self): 
    print("Hello my name is " + self.name) 
 
p1 = Person("John", 36) 
p1.myfunc() 
 
The self Parameter 
The self parameter is a reference to the current instance of the class, and is used to 
access variables that belongs to the class. 
--- page 4 ---
Modify Object Properties 
You can modify properties on objects like this: 
Example  
Set the age of p1 to 40: 
p1.age = 40 
 
Delete Object Properties 
You can delete properties on objects by using the del keyword: 
Example  
Delete the age property from the p1 object: 
del p1.age 
 
Delete Objects 
You can delete objects by using the del keyword: 
Example  
Delete the p1 object: 
del p1 
 
The pass Statement 
class definitions cannot be empty, but if you for some reason have a class definition with 
no content, put in the pass statement to avoid getting an error. 
class Person: 
 pass

+Lab 2.1 - Reviewing a Requirements Document
+Student: Albert Muratbaev
+Defect letters: C contradiction, A ambiguous, T not testable, N not a requirement,
+                W wrong type.
+
+================================================================================
+EXERCISE 1 - The TTPU library system
+================================================================================
+
+1.1 The four contradictions
+
+Pair            | Why they cannot live together
+FR-01 & FR-02   | The maximum is 5 books, but FR-02 permits a 6th book.
+FR-04 & FR-06   | A reference book may not leave the building, yet FR-06 renews it
+                | online like an ordinary take-home loan.
+FR-07 & FR-08   | The same reminder is required both 2 days BEFORE the due date and
+                | only AFTER the book is already late.
+FR-16 & FR-17   | Keeping the full borrowing history forever conflicts with deleting
+                | identifying personal data 1 year after departure.
+
+1.2 The three lines that are not requirements
+
+ID      | What it really is      | Where it belongs
+FR-13   | Design decision        | In the design document, after technical evaluation.
+        | ("The database shall   |
+        | be MySQL 8.")          |
+FR-18   | Business goal          | In the library business plan or project plan; measured by
+        | (buying 200 books)     | the department, not by the software.
+NFR-03  | Impossible promise     | Nowhere; replace it with a measurable reliability target.
+        | ("never fail")         | (see 1.3)
+
+1.3 The four untestable lines, repaired
+
+ID      | Corrected requirement (with a number and a unit)                 | How it is tested
+FR-09   | NFR-04 A first-year student shall find and reserve a known       | Ask 5 first-year students to reserve a named available
+        | available book in no more than 4 clicks after sign-in.           | book and count the clicks of each.
+FR-14   | NFR-05 Search results shall appear within 2 seconds for a        | Run 100 searches against 50,000 records with 100
+        | catalogue of 50,000 books and 100 concurrent users.              | users and measure every response time.
+FR-15   | NFR-06 The first page of search results shall appear within      | Execute 100 representative searches and time the
+        | 2 seconds for 95% of them.                                       | first result page each time.
+NFR-03  | NFR-03 The system shall have at least 99.5% availability during  | Compare monitoring downtime with the scheduled
+        | library working hours each semester.                             | working hours of the semester.
+
+1.4 The four contradictions, repaired (8 requirements in total)
+
+FR-01  The system shall allow a registered student to borrow at most 5 books without special approval.
+FR-02  The system shall allow a librarian to approve one additional book, increasing the
+       limit to 6 for that loan.
+FR-04  Books marked "reference" shall be used only inside the library and shall not create
+       a take-home loan.
+FR-06  The system shall not offer online renewal for a book marked "reference".
+FR-07  The system shall send an e-mail reminder 2 days before the due date for a loan that
+       is not returned.
+FR-08  The system shall send one overdue e-mail at 09:00 on the first day after the due date
+       if the book remains unreturned.
+FR-16  The system shall retain borrowing transactions in anonymised form indefinitely for
+       statistics.
+FR-17  The system shall delete or anonymise data identifying a student within 1 year after
+       the student leaves the university.
+
+================================================================================
+EXERCISE 2 - The TTPU canteen pre-order system
+================================================================================
+
+2.1 The full review table (exactly 12 defect rows)
+
+ID      | Defect  | What exactly is wrong                                                          | Corrected line (or "delete")
+FR-03   | C       | Contradicts FR-02: payment cannot be both before cooking and at collection.    | The student shall pay in the application before the order is sent to the kitchen; cash payment is not supported in version 1.
+FR-06   | C       | Changes until 11:45 contradict FR-05 cooking starting at 11:30.                | A student shall change an order until 11:25 while its status is Not started.
+FR-08   | C       | Contradicts FR-09: a dish is either orderable with 0 portions or not.          | delete (FR-09 keeps the single stock rule)
+FR-11   | C       | Immediate sending contradicts FR-12 sending one list at 11:00.                 | Each confirmed order shall appear on the kitchen screen within 5 seconds after payment.
+FR-12   | C       | Conflicts with FR-11 and can delay the kitchen up to 30 minutes.               | At 11:00 the system shall send a summary of all confirmed orders in addition to the 5-second individual updates.
+FR-13   | A/T/W   | "Without the internet" is ambiguous and unmeasurable, and it is non-functional | NFR-05 The kitchen screen shall show cached confirmed orders for up to 30 minutes after internet loss.
+        |         | written in the functional list.                                                |
+FR-15   | C       | English-only messages contradict FR-14 three interface languages.              | Messages shall be shown in the language the user selects from Uzbek, Russian and English.
+FR-17   | N       | Python/Django is a design decision, not required behaviour.                    | delete (evaluate technology in the design document)
+FR-18   | N       | Reducing food waste by 30% is a business goal, not software behaviour.         | delete (move to the project plan; measure via reports)
+FR-19   | T/W     | "Secure" is unmeasurable and non-functional in a functional list.              | NFR-04 Payment data shall use TLS 1.3 and no card number or CVV shall be stored.

+NFR-03  | T       | "Easy to use" is subjective with no measure.                                   | NFR-03 A first-year student shall place a standard order in at most 6 clicks without training.
+
+2.2 The five missing requirements (FR-21 - FR-25)
+
+FR-21  The system shall mark a paid order Uncollected if it is not collected within 60
+       minutes after it is marked Ready, and shall keep the money on the student's account.
+FR-22  The system shall return a cancelled card payment to the original payment method
+       within 5 working days.
+FR-23  The system shall show declared allergens for every dish before the student confirms
+       the order.
+FR-24  The system shall prevent ordering on dates marked Closed in the manager calendar
+       and shall show the next opening time.
+FR-25  Only an authenticated user with the Manager role shall open the manager screen
+       and view the daily revenue.
+
+2.3 The SDLC question - when should each defect have been found (four rows)
+
+ID     | Found now          | Should have been found          | If found only after release (cost chart)
+FR-03  | Requirements       | Requirement gathering /         | About 50-100 units: payment flow, UI, accounting and user training
+       | review             | review (written the same day)   | would all need correction after real payments had been made.
+FR-06  | Requirements       | Requirement review              | About 50 units: students could change food that is already cooking,
+       | review             |                                 | causing refunds and wasted meals.
+FR-11  | Requirements       | Requirement review              | About 50-100 units: the kitchen screen and the cooks' workflow
+       | review             |                                 | would need redesign and retraining after the kitchen already trusts it.
+FR-15  | Requirements       | Requirement review /            | About 50 units: messages and translations across every screen would
+       | review             | prototyping                     | need rework after students complain in their own language.
+
+2.4 Use case "Student orders a meal"
+
+Actor: Student.
+Precondition: the student is signed in, ordering is open (08:00-11:00), and at least one
+dish has portions available.
+
+Main flow:
+1. The system shows today's menu, prices, available portions and allergens.    (FR-01, FR-07, FR-23)
+2. The student selects one or more available dishes.
+3. The system shows the order summary and the total amount.
+4. The student confirms and chooses application payment.
+5. The payment service confirms the payment.                                   (FR-02)
+6. The system assigns a daily-unique order number.                             (FR-10)
+7. The order appears on the kitchen screen within 5 seconds.                   (corrected FR-11)
+8. The system shows the order number and confirmation to the student.
+
+Alternative flow - payment fails: at step 5, if payment is rejected or times out, the
+system creates no confirmed kitchen order, shows the failure reason and lets the student
+retry once or cancel.
+
+Postcondition: a paid order with a unique number is stored and visible to the kitchen, or
+- if payment failed - no confirmed order exists and no meal is cooked.
+
+Traceability (start of the matrix): this use case covers FR-01, FR-02, FR-04, FR-07,
+FR-09, FR-10, corrected FR-11, FR-21, FR-23 and NFR-01.
